si_4_title.answer: A 10-Year Longitudinal Study of Brain Cortical Thickness in People with FirstEpisode Psychosis Using Normative Models

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Hierarchical Bayesian regression (HBR) was used to estimate normative models for 150 ROIs. This approach accommodates inter-site variation and scanner effects.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: We used the Hierarchical Bayesian regression (HBR) approach for normative modeling, which efficiently accommodates inter-site variation and provides computational scaling... We estimated a normative model for each region of interest (ROI, n = 150) in the Freesurfer Destrieux atlas, using HBR with age as a covariate, and sex and scanner id as batch effects, to predict CT.

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Cortical Thickness (CT) measures parcellated using the Destrieux atlas (150 ROIs).
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: T1-weighted structural MRI scans were preprocessed through Freesurfer (version 5.3), and CT measures were parcellated using the Destrieux atlas... We estimated a normative model... to predict CT.
nm2_2_response_variable.location: Berthet2025.pdf.md: Methods / MRI Data Acquisition and Analysis & Normative Modeling

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Age was used as a covariate. Sex and scanner id were used as batch effects. The model accommodates inter-site variation (Site).
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: using HBR with age as a covariate, and sex and scanner id as batch effects, to predict CT... Accommodating site variation in neuroimaging data using normative and hierarchical Bayesian models.
